question: Why did our churn rate spike last month?
sql:
WITH last_order AS (
  SELECT user_id, MAX(created_at) AS last_order_at
  FROM orders
  WHERE status <> 'Cancelled'
  GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', TIMESTAMP_ADD(last_order_at, INTERVAL 90 DAY)) AS churn_month,
       COUNT(*) AS churned_customers
FROM last_order
WHERE last_order_at < TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
GROUP BY churn_month
ORDER BY churn_month DESC
LIMIT 12
report: Our definition of churn: a customer has churned when 90 days pass without an order, and they are counted in the month in which the 90th day falls. Only months whose 90th day has already passed count: a customer whose last order is less than 90 days old has not churned yet, so a month that has not happened is never reported as churn. To explain a spike, compare the churned customers of that month with the month before: what they last bought (brand and category), how they were acquired (traffic source) and where they live. A spike often traces back to one large acquisition cohort reaching the 90-day mark.
